references.text: The Book of Ruth shows how Ruth, a Moabite woman, was incorporated into the people of Israel and became an ancestor of King David, despite the ban on Moabites in the assembly of the Lord.
Nehemiah refers directly to this law when he read from the Book of Moses and found the ban on Ammonites and Moabites in the assembly of God, separating all foreigners from Israel.
Lamentations mentions how the assembly of the Lord was desecrated, which connects to the term 'assembly of the Lord' (קְהַל יְהוָה) used in Deuteronomy.
Zechariah prophesies that a 'bastard' (mamzer) will dwell in Ashdod, using the same Hebrew word found in Deuteronomy 23:3.
Isaiah speaks of foreigners who cling to the Lord not saying that the Lord has separated them from his people, showing an extended grace beyond the strict law.
